sentences.text: This dinosaur measured between 6 and 7 meters in length and weighed roughly 1.3 metric tons.
It moved on two legs with its body trunk tilted upward.
The animal possessed a small head equipped with a beak and a long, slender neck.
Robust forelimbs featured three fingers with large claws, while the feet had four toes.
Its lower jaw curved downward at the front, and some hindmost teeth displayed extra cutting edges.
A joint Soviet-Mongolian expedition found a partial skeleton at the Amtgay locality in 1973.
Paleontologist Altangerel Perle named the species Segnosaurus galbinensis in 1979.
The generic name translates to 'slow lizard,' combining Latin and Ancient Greek roots.
Therizinosaurs like this species likely used their long limbs and necks for browsing and had large guts to process food.
The family Segnosauridae is now considered a junior synonym of Therizinosauridae.
Perle initially classified the group as theropods based on similarities in the jaw and front teeth.
He also suggested that Segnosaurus and Therizinosaurus formed a family distinct from Deinocheiridae.
However, Gregory S. Paul later concluded in 1984 that segnosaurs were derived, late-surviving Cretaceous prosauropods lacking theropod features.
The animal lived in southeastern Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 102 to 86 million years ago.
It is debated how widespread the distinguishing anatomical features of Segnosaurus are among therizinosaurs due to incomplete preservation in most genera.
Researchers cannot determine if bone growth over the 14th tooth socket in the right jaw of the holotype resulted from injury or disease, as the teeth there are too damaged to assess the effect.
Scientists also cannot conclude whether the triple cutting edges on the left jaw teeth are a normal feature or a result of pathology, unlike the right jaw which shows signs of injury or disease.

It is debated whether pelvic similarities between Segnosaurus and Nothronychus result from a shared common ancestor exclusive to derived therizinosaurids or from the retention of basal features lost in other relatives.
